function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
**Reykjavík – the clear winner for an ice‑hockey‑focused trip to Iceland**

| Why Reykjavík stands out | Details |
|---------------------------|---------|
| **Largest and most modern rink** | *Egilshöll* (also known as the “Ice Palace”) is the biggest indoor arena in Iceland. It hosts the national team’s home games, the Icelandic Hockey League (IHL) matches, and international tournaments. |
| **National team hub** | The Icelandic national team trains and plays most of its home fixtures in Reykjavík. Visiting the rink gives you a chance to see the team in action and meet local players. |
| **Icelandic Hockey League** | The IHL’s top teams (e.g., *Skautafélag Reykjavíkur*, *Skautafélag Akureyrar*) play their home games in Reykjavík. The league runs from late October to early April, so you can catch a game during the season. |
| **Convenient travel & amenities** | As the capital, Reykjavík has the country’s main airport (Keflavík International), plenty of hotels, restaurants, and public transport. |
| **Cultural blend** | After a game, you can explore Reykjavík’s vibrant nightlife, museums, and culinary scene—making it a well‑rounded travel experience. |

---

### If you’re looking for a more intimate, local vibe

| City | Highlights |
|------|------------|
| **Akureyri** | Iceland’s “Capital of the North.” The *Akureyri Ice Rink* hosts local league games and community events. It’s a smaller, cozy venue where you can mingle with locals and see grassroots hockey. |
| **Húsavík** | Home to *Skautafélag Húsavíkur*, a club that competes in the IHL. The town’s rink is smaller but offers a friendly atmosphere and a chance to experience hockey in a quieter setting. |

---

### Practical tips for your visit

| Tip | Explanation |
|-----|-------------|
| **When to go** | The IHL season runs Oct–Apr. If you want to see the national team, plan for a weekend during the season. |
| **Tickets** | Buy online via the club’s website or at the arena box office. Prices are modest (≈ $10–$20). |
| **Getting around** | Reykjavík’s public bus system (Strætó) covers most attractions. For Akureyri, consider renting a car or using local buses. |
| **Accommodation** | Reykjavík offers a range from budget hostels to boutique hotels. In Akureyri, look for guesthouses or small hotels for a cozy stay. |
| **Language** | English is widely spoken, especially in Reykjavík. A few Icelandic phrases (“Takk” – thank you, “Góðan daginn” – good day) go a long way. |
| **Weather** | Pack layers. Even in summer, evenings can be cool, and in winter, it’s cold—especially near the rink. |

---

### Quick contact info

| Club | Website | Phone |
|------|---------|-------|
| Skautafélag Reykjavíkur | https://www.sr.is/ | +354 555 5555 |
| Skautafélag Akureyrar | https://www.sak.is/ | +354 666 6666 |
| Skautafélag Húsavíkur | https://www.sh.is/ | +354 777 7777 |

*(Numbers are illustrative; check the websites for current contact details.)*

---

**Bottom line:** If you’re looking for the best overall experience—largest arena, national team, easy travel—Reykjavík is the place to go. If you prefer a quieter, community‑focused atmosphere, Akureyri or Húsavík are excellent alternatives. Happy travels and enjoy the puck‑action!
